clue.text: Left and hurried back, coming in to make meal of jam

indicators.note: coming in to says the pieces before it are placed inside the word for a meal

parts.note: sup is an old word for a supper or meal

indicators.note: back says the word for hurried is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: hurried means ran

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off and returns to turn a pot of preserve into a feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAN into NAR; add L and 'coming in to' puts NARL inside SUP. 'Jam' looks like the fruit preserve but is the traffic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl-up is a tangle of stuck traffic, the same as a traffic jam.

clue.text: Fancifully in the mood for dismissing a lot?

definitions.text: Fancifully in the mood for dismissing a lot?

parts.words: Fancifully in the mood for dismissing a lot?
parts.note: read fancifully, the word is like playful or boastful: full of the urge to fire people, as a boss keen on giving staff the boot might be; plainly it is a large quantity held in a bag

explanation.surface: A boss feels whimsically eager to fire a large number of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancifully' flags that the word is split into SACK (dismiss) and -FUL (full of), while its real meaning is the amount a sack holds, a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sackful is as much as a large bag holds, a big quantity of anything.

clue.text: Bald Henry left, inspiration being impossible?

indicators.note: left here means gone away, so the letter for Henry departs from the word for bald

parts.note: bald means hairless
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A bald man named Henry has walked out, leaving no hope of a creative spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' looks like creative genius, but here it is breathing in, impossible where there is no air.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiration in the physical sense is drawing breath, which cannot happen in a space without oxygen.

clue.text: Balanced lines about the first lady

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the lines go round the first lady

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so lines gives LL
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Neat lines of verse are written about the original woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something level is even and balanced, with no side higher than the other.

clue.text: Possibly nine plus one made by Gower?

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be put into another order

parts.note: one gives A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone sums nine plus one, a calculation credited to the poet Gower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges NINE PLUS into PENINSUL; A for 'one' ends it. Gower is the peninsula west of Swansea in Wales, not the medieval poet the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gower is a stretch of land in south Wales jutting into the sea, surrounded on three sides by water.

clue.text: Material one removed from architectural column?

indicators.note: removed says the letter for one is taken out of the column word

parts.note: a pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Building stuff is taken off an ornamental pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaster is a building substance spread on walls and ceilings.

clue.text: One in posture showing balance

indicators.note: in says the letter for one sits inside the word for posture

parts.note: a pose is a posture held, as for a portrait
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gymnast holding a position displays steadiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is steadiness and composure, a state of being balanced.

clue.text: Logical end of Spenser narrative could be so?

definitions.text: Logical end of Spenser narrative could be so?

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become a different word when rearranged

parts.note: the last two letters of the name Spenser are E and R

explanation.surface: A reader concludes Spenser's long poem logically had to be a symbolic tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges LOGICAL plus ER, the final two letters of Spenser. The whole clue also defines: The Faerie Queene, Spenser's epic, is famously an extended allegory.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's Faerie Queene is a symbolic poem in which characters stand for virtues, the classic case of a narrative with hidden meanings.

clue.text: Double-act performed, containing old piece of music

indicators.note: containing says the jumbled letters hold the letter for old
performed suggests the letters are worked into a new order, as a piece is performed
double says the word act is written twice

explanation.surface: A comedy duo puts on an act that includes a vintage tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' gives ACTACT, which 'performed' rearranges to TCCATA, and 'containing' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a keyboard composition showing off fast fingerwork, a type of musical work.

clue.text: Perhaps embarrassed about exorbitant rate for tyre?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the colour word goes round the jumbled rate

parts.note: embarrassed people may go red in the face, so this is an example of the colour

indicators.note: exorbitant literally means out of orbit, off its track, so the word rate goes astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist blushes at the excessive price charged for a tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exorbitant' rearranges RATE into TREA, which RED goes 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is a worn tyre given a new tread, so a recycled tyre.

clue.text: Motoring organisation backs one at front of convoy

indicators.note: backs here means goes in reverse, so the motoring body's letters are read the other way

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation
one gives A, the indefinite article
van means the front, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: A breakdown service supports a single vehicle leading a line of traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns RAC into CAR. The RAC is a British roadside-recovery club, like the AAA in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a group of travellers or vehicles moving together in a line.

clue.text: It's said to give rise to contraband

indicators.note: said says the word is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: to elicit is to draw out or bring about

explanation.surface: Rumours are reported to be behind smuggled goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraband goods are forbidden ones, unlawful to trade.

clue.text: Fish in European country one can sell to anybody

indicators.note: in says the fish sits inside the country's name

parts.note: France is a country in Europe
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A fishmonger in a continental nation can market the catch to all comers.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance is self-employed and offers work to any client rather than one employer.

clue.text: Greek prayer which is for the departed?

parts.note: Ave, short for Ave Maria, is a prayer to the Virgin Mary

explanation.surface: An Orthodox prayer is said for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is the burial place made for someone who has died.

clue.text: Composer featuring in catalogue we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound and entered with a different spelling

parts.note: a catalogue is a list of items

explanation.surface: A musician appears in an inventory being read out.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian virtuoso pianist who wrote the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: A1 cricket bags which can set precedents?

parts.note: a Test match is cricket at the highest international level
bags means cases, as luggage

explanation.surface: First-rate cricket kit bags that will set the standard for others.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international game of cricket, the top grade of the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal disputes whose rulings decide later similar lawsuits are known by this name.

clue.text: Deceitful junior employee?

explanation.surface: A sly assistant on the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: an under-hand is a hand, or worker, under another.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceitful dealing is sly and secret; a junior worker is a hand placed under a senior one.

clue.text: Potential merit in minor damage or injury?

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the word for minor damage

parts.note: a dent is a small bit of damage to a surface

indicators.note: potential says the letters are what merit might become when rearranged

explanation.surface: A small scratch might still be counted as harm or hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potential' rearranges MERIT into TRIME, which goes 'in' DENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is harm or loss suffered by someone, a hurt.

clue.text: Senior teacher's sour? It's a great advantage

parts.note: a head is the headteacher, the senior teacher at a school
tart means sharp or sour in taste

explanation.surface: A school principal is grumpy, which gives pupils plenty to exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting ahead of rivals gives an early lead, a big edge in a race.

clue.text: House crime bust by ancient linesman?

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of crime are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglary is foiled by an old-time line judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' rearranges CRIME into MERIC. The 'ancient linesman' is not a sports official but Homer, the Greek poet who wrote many lines of epic verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means belonging to Homer, the Greek poet of the Iliad and Odyssey, writer of countless lines.

clue.text: Wrong names by one? A case of this perhaps?

definitions.text: Wrong names by one? A case of this perhaps?

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of names are put in a faulty order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone keeps getting names wrong, maybe a sign of memory loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges NAMES into AMNES, then I for 'one' and the A of 'A case'; the whole clue also defines, since muddling names is typical of memory loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Memory loss leads people to forget or confuse names.

clue.text: One wades right into corporal punishment

indicators.note: into says the letter for right goes inside the word for the punishment

parts.note: the cane was a stick used to beat pupils as punishment

explanation.surface: Someone splashes through water right into a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One wades' looks like a person paddling but describes the long-legged bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane is a tall long-legged bird that stands and walks in shallow water.

clue.text: A female insect is unyielding

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, such as a mare or ewe
an ant is a small insect

explanation.surface: A queen ant refuses to give way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adamant means being firm and refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: A runner has to take English and needs one to explain text

parts.note: a runner in crosswords is a river, and the Exe is a river in Devon
to get is to take or obtain

explanation.surface: A sprinter must study English and needs a tutor to interpret a passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' looks like an athlete but means a river; the Exe flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An exegete interprets scripture or other writings, critically analysing passages.

parts.note: ornate means elaborately decorated
I is the Roman numeral for one
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A single American serviceman makes an elaborate beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being.

clue.text: There could be nothing like one's watering hole

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
as means like, in the same way
one is I, so one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: A drinker says no bar is quite like their local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watering hole' suggests a pub, but here it is a fertile place with water in a desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert spring where animals and travellers come to drink is literally a place for watering.

clue.text: One uses flexible spring

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: flexible says the letters of uses bend into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone applies a bendy coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow out or emerge, as water springs from a source.

clue.text: Limiting island holidays does not give one a clear run

definitions.text: does not give one a clear run

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on each side, so the holidays word encloses the island

parts.note: rests are breaks from work

explanation.surface: Restricting trips to islands blocks a smooth journey.
explanation.definitionFit: One who opposes or withstands someone puts obstacles in their way.

clue.text: Enthral in Parisian valse with gliding movement

parts.note: en is French for in, as spoken in Paris

indicators.note: the gliding steps of a waltz suggest the letters of valse moving into a new position

explanation.surface: A dancer in Paris captivates the room with a smooth waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with gliding movement' rearranges VALSE (French for waltz) into SLAVE, after EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral originally meant to make a thrall, a bondsman, so both mean to put in bondage.

clue.text: Some research assistance needed to produce a frame

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of help with research is required to build a framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base structure of a vehicle onto which the body is built.

clue.text: Support for board's formulation of letters

indicators.note: formulation means making up, so the letters of the word are made up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A notice board's mount is built from correspondence.
